 agents for Airflow site

messages.subject:
[CONTRIBUTION OPPORTUNITY] llms.txt and Markdown docs for coding
 agents for Airflow site
messages.body:
Hi all,

More and more people write Dags with coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor,
Copilot, Codex), and those agents read our docs as HTML. A provider guide
page is about 150 KB of HTML for about 20 KB of content, and fetch tools
often summarise it down to a paragraph, code samples included. Pydantic AI,
Ray, Camel, Astronomer and most of the popular sites & project publish an
llms.txt index plus a Markdown copy of each page. We publish neither.

I've opened an issue with a plan and a working proof of concept, starting
with the Common AI provider docs:

https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/74376

It has three parts:

1. Docs build: generate page.html.md next to every page, plus llms.txt and
llms-full.txt, using sphinx-llm and a small extension. The proof of concept
builds cleanly for Common AI with no change in build time.
2. Publishing: a couple of guards in breeze so stable/ always has the
Markdown copies.
3. Serving: Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot and OpenCode already send "Accept:
text/markdown" on every fetch. A short .htaccess rule in airflow-site can
answer those requests with the Markdown copy, so agents get it from the
URLs they already use. I tested this on airflow.staged.apache.org; ASF's
Fastly cache keeps the HTML and Markdown answers apart.

*I won't have time to build this or to review it, so it needs an owner who
can see it through, including reviews.* The issue lists what's done, what's
left, and the rollout constraints. It needs a committer, or a contributor
pairing with one: testing the airflow-site change on staging, publishing
docs and checking the live rollout all need committer access.

This would be a high impact change, so thanks in advance for whoever picks
it up.

Regards,
Kaxil

> > > often summarise it down to a paragraph, code samples included. Pydantic
> > AI,
> > > Ray, Camel, Astronomer and most of the popular sites & project publish
> an
> > > llms.txt index plus a Markdown copy of each page. We publish neither.
> > >
> > > I've opened an issue with a plan and a working proof of concept,
> starting
> > > with the Common AI provider docs:
> > >
> > > https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fapache%2Fairflow%2Fissues%2F74376&data=05%7C02%7Cdavid.blain%40infrabel.be%7C8b25c7e9d32b4dfa939808df23fdc912%7Cb82bc314ab8e4d6fb18946f02e1f27f2%7C0%7C0%7C639269245055449115%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=rHwv1AaT41G789YkOXh7cINsukGuOc7fUn0%2FItMXHyo%3D&reserved=0<https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/74376>
> > >

> > and

> > concept
> > > builds cleanly for Common AI with no change in build time.
> > > 2. Publishing: a couple of guards in breeze so stable/ always has the
> > > Markdown copies.
> > > 3. Serving: Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot and OpenCode already send
> > "Accept:
> > > text/markdown" on every fetch. A short .htaccess rule in airflow-site
> can
> > > answer those requests with the Markdown copy, so agents get it from the
> > > URLs they already use. I tested this on airflow.staged.apache.org;
> ASF's
> > > Fastly cache keeps the HTML and Markdown answers apart.
> > >
> > > *I won't have time to build this or to review it, so it needs an owner
> > who
> > > can see it through, including reviews.* The issue lists what's done,
> > what's
> > > left, and the rollout constraints. It needs a committer, or a
> contributor
> > > pairing with one: testing the airflow-site change on staging,
> publishing
> > > docs and checking the live rollout all need committer access.
> > >
> > > This would be a high impact change, so thanks in advance for whoever
> > picks
> > > it up.
> > >
> > > Regards,
> > > Kaxil
> > >
> >
>
